10/15 we tested your earnings plan on stocks (buy after a company beats its profit forecast, on a small dip). It first looked great (+89% to +122%), but those tests only used stocks we already knew did well. On the honest stock list it lost 14%, dipped 32%, did worse than just holding the stock market (+72%), and even worse than random buys. No real edge.
10/15 daily check of the main plan (R4-C), last 12 months: +10.6% with an 8.5% worst dip in 9 trades. Turning one setting down a little (0.9×) made it lose 11% instead, so it's touchy.

10/15 test with up to 50 trades a year allowed: it didn't help once fees were counted. Most plans came out the same. The new-high plan made more (+101%) but still dipped 24%. The full-size breakout plan only just squeezed under the 20% limit by luck. The bets-sized-by-jumpiness breakout plan is still the one to watch, at +40% with a 13% worst dip.
The testing tool had a bug that faked some losses. It's fixed, and every test was re-run.
The big test covers 2022 to today and checks each plan on data it never saw while we picked its settings.
To pass, a plan has to make money, never dip more than 20%, beat just holding Bitcoin, and make enough trades for us to trust the result.
Every test here uses pretend money. Only the live bot uses real money.
headline: None of the plans is ready yet. The one to watch is the breakout plan with smaller bets: in pretend trading it turned $1,000 into about $1,420, and its worst dip was 13%. But it lost money in half of the test periods and in the last 6 months, so it stays on paper. Your new earnings plan for stocks was also tested today: on an honest stock list it has no real edge.

long.name: ⭐ Breakout, bets sized by how jumpy the price is
long.kid: The safer version of the breakout plan. Its worst dip stayed under 20%, but it lost money in 5 of 10 test periods and in the last 6 months, which it never saw while we picked its settings. It also trades about 23 times a year, which is more than your limit of about 15. We're watching it, not using it.

long.name: Old main plan (R4-C)
long.kid: Our old main plan. It made money over 5 years but at one point was down 30%, which is too scary, and it falls apart when its settings are nudged.

long.name: Old plan, no filter (R3)
long.kid: The old plan without its safety filter. It lost money.

long.name: Moving-average cross
long.kid: Buys when the short-term average rises above the long-term one. It made money, but its worst dip (37%) was too deep.

long.name: New-high trend
long.kid: Buys when the price hits a new high. It made the most money, but the dips were too deep (25%) and it traded too often.

long.name: Breakout above 200-day average
long.kid: Buys when the price breaks above its 200-day average. It's the closest to passing, and its results stay the same when its settings are nudged. Its worst dip was 21.8%, just over our 20% limit. Next we'll test it with smaller bets.

long.name: Buy the dip (RSI)
long.kid: The 'buy the dip' plan. It stayed under the safety limit, but it made only 20 trades in about 5 years and lost money in most test periods, so we can't trust it yet.

long.name: Just hold Bitcoin
long.kid: Just buying Bitcoin and holding it. It barely made money and at one point lost 69%. This is the plan to beat.

oneyear.name: R4-C (our main plan)
oneyear.kid: Our best plan. Over a year of pretend trading it grew $1,000 to about $1,150, and the worst dip along the way was about 8%.

oneyear.name: R3 (no chop filter)
oneyear.kid: The same plan without its safety filter. It lost about $140 on every $1,000. The real-money bot uses rules close to this one.

oneyear.name: Test A
oneyear.kid: Lost money, about the same as R3.

oneyear.name: Test D
oneyear.kid: It made a little money (+4%) with tiny dips, but it traded 31 times in one year, which is far more than your limit of about 15.

oneyear.name: Test R1
oneyear.kid: Came out exactly the same as R3, so its extra rule never actually did anything.
